scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: HELP!! Part of our network has FALLEN OFF THE MAP
after one of the boxes restarted. The clever people say the two halves were
held together by some kind of INVISIBLE BRIDGE, which sounds made up to me,
and something around it must be wrong. I always said you can't hold a network
together with something invisible!! Could someone look at it so the far areas
are reachable again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
r8 is an OSPF ABR connected to the backbone (Area 0) exclusively through a virtual link that transits Area 1 (the "invisible bridge" the ticket references). The virtual link itself is operationally healthy — both r4 and r8 show the VLINK0 adjacency as Full. The fault lies in r8's backbone LSDB: r8's Area 0 database contains 72 LSAs while r4's Area 0 database contains 73. The single missing entry is the ASBR-summary (type 4) LSA for the EIGRP ASBR r11 (router-ID 112.1.1.1), which r1 originates in Area 0 with metric 10. That LSA is fully present and valid on r4, but FRR does not propagate type-4 ASBR-summary LSAs to a virtual-link endpoint's Area 0 database — r8 never receives it.

Without the type-4 LSA in any area, r8 cannot compute a path to the EIGRP ASBR and therefore installs zero OSPF external (OE2) routes. Direct evidence: `show ip route 102.1.1.0/24` on r8 returns "Network not in table"; ping from r8 to 102.1.1.1 returns "Network is unreachable". The reverse direction also fails: r12 pings r8's loopback 18.1.1.1 with 100% loss because r8 cannot reply — it has no route to r12's source address. Root cause: r8 restarted (adjacency up-times of ~1 min vs 3–4 min for unaffected routers), and the startup configuration lost the static default route (`ip route add default via 58.1.1.1`) that previously worked around FRR's virtual-link type-4 LSA limitation. Corrective fix: restore a static default route on r8 pointing to 58.1.1.1 (r5) so it can reach EIGRP-domain prefixes via the backbone; for a permanent architectural fix, assign r8 a physical Area 0 interface to eliminate the virtual-link dependency.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup notes the r4<->r8 virtual-link is up but does not state that PC0 can reach PC12 across the multi-area fabric at baseline, so it fails the full bonus-note requirement.

The agent's conclusions about a missing type-4 LSA and resulting routing absence on r8 are mostly supported by the investigation outputs (virtual-link up, missing OSPF external routes on r8, and failed ping tests). However, stronger causal claims (FRR not propagating type‑4 LSAs to virtual-link endpoints and that r8 lost a static default on restart) are not directly evidenced in the log and are thus speculative.
